messages:
Emily: quick sync - we've got divergent behavior across SDKs when the platform routes to a lower-capacity model or different region. need a minimal, implementable contract.
Sam: agreed. python sometimes surfaces Retry-After, node throws Error, some clients return 200 with a warning object, others just return the downgraded output with no hint.
Rohit: can we get a canonical example from prod so we know what to standardize on?
Emily: prod snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Fallback: model=redwood-m-small;reason=pool_limit
{"model":"redwood-m-small","tokens_used":43,"warning":"served lower-capacity model due to temporary capacity"}
```
Marta: product note - if SDKs silently hide fallback (200 + output), console must still ingest a clear fallback metric. customers need to correlate quality drops with fallbacks.
Kevin: telemetry proposal: emit metric names `inference.fallback.total` and `inference.fallback.by_reason`, tag with `fallback_model` and `route`. also emit a non-PII event for the incident stream.
Rohit: http semantics idea: return 200 for successful outputs even if downgraded, 429 for client limits, 503 for systemic infra failures that prevented any output. 200+fallback-ok if header and metric exist.
Emily: SDK surface suggestion: add `response.fallback` typed as null or `{ model: string, reason: string, retry_after_seconds: number | null, user_friendly_reason: string }`. also emit non-fatal Warning (not exception) and a visible console log line.
Sam: +1. Keep `X-Redwood-Fallback` header for backwards compatibility with simple HTTP clients. header should be short: `model=redwood-m-small;reason=capacity;retry=30`.
Rohit: security constraint: do NOT expose internal pool ids or routing keys. map internal codes (e.g., `pool_limit`) -> `capacity` in user_friendly_reason. internal telemetry should keep the raw code for debugging.
Marta: suggested customer-facing copy for SDK warning/console card: "Reduced-capability model used due to temporary capacity constraints. Consider reserved capacity for consistent performance." Short, actionable.
Kevin: also capture whether fallback choice was cost-driven vs capacity-driven vs policy-driven. propose reason taxonomy: `capacity`, `quota`, `policy`, `region_failover`, `degraded_node`. these map from internal codes.
Emily: rollout plan: (1) publish minimal contract doc, (2) land SDKs behind an opt-in flag `fallback_visibility=beta`, (3) console starts ingesting `inference.fallback.*` metrics, (4) flip opt-in to default after 2 SDK releases.
Rohit: will update Node/Python SDKs: parse header, populate fallback object, emit metric event to statsd, and add unit tests.
Sam: I'll update devex quickstart and add example snippets for handling `response.fallback` and the Warning event.
Marta: I'll prototype a console card: fallback rate by route + sparkline, and an alert policy for >5% fallback rate sustained 5m.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: eng-platform/fallback-minicontract -> canary 5% @ 2025-06-12T09:00:00Z
Kevin: action recap: Rohit: SDKs & tests, Sam: docs & examples, Marta: console card & alerts, Emily: finalize contract text. objections?
Rohit: none from infra.
Emily: none. thanks :thumbsup:
Sam: leaving a note to keep the SDKs small - don't change other response shapes.
Marta: and we should autopopulate console metrics even for legacy clients by parsing the header at the ingress proxy.
Kevin: ok. i'll add a short telemetry schema to the contract doc (metric names + tags + sample event).
Emily: great. will publish the contract PR today and tag the SDK teams. thanks all.
